## [CRITICAL] items

### [CRITICAL] BLD — `applyExpansionOverrides()` clobbers LI5's global of the same name

**Where:** `js/games/bld.js` — `function applyExpansionOverrides()` (line ~1273) + its call in `bldStartGame()` (line ~315); collides with `js/games/li5.js` `function applyExpansionOverrides()` (line ~162)
**What:** BLD declares a global no-op `applyExpansionOverrides()`. LI5 already owns that global name (its real Secret Mode override reader). `bld.js` loads after `li5.js`, so BLD's hoisted top-level declaration overwrites LI5's on `window`. LI5's `startGame()` (line 176) then calls BLD's no-op instead of its own function.
**Why it matters:** In Secret Mode, Like I'm Five silently stops applying its forced expansion settings (timer, rounds, taboo count, penalty mode, skip, Sylly). No error — LI5 just plays with the wrong settings. This is the exact collision the JEC naming note warns about (JEC avoided it via `jecApplyExpansionOverrides()`).
**Fix:** Rename BLD's hook to `bldApplyExpansionOverrides()` and update the one call site in `bldStartGame()`. BLD's version is a no-op, so the rename is behaviourally inert for BLD and restores LI5's override.
**Verify:** `grep -n "function applyExpansionOverrides" js/games/*.js` returns only `li5.js`. Enter Secret Mode, start LI5, confirm the forced expansion timer/rounds take effect.
**Rule violated:** `game-identities.md` § JEC naming-collision note; `definitions.md` § Function Naming (`[abbr]*()` prefix)
**Logged:** `bld-implementation-notes.md` Bug 16

## [BUG] items

### [BUG] Engine — 20 overlays are never hidden by any reset path

**Where:** `js/engine.js` — `resetToLobby()` (and the per-game reset functions it delegates to: `resetSyllySignals`, `resetSecretMode`, `resetYouGetIt`, `resetLateToTheParty`, `natResetState`, `dsdResetState`, `bldResetState`, `gthResetState`)
**What:** These overlays are hidden only by their own close/cancel buttons — no reset path touches them: `settings-overlay`, `deck-panel`, `skip-turn-overlay` (LI5); `gm-settings-overlay`, `gm-near-sync-overlay`, `gm-boost-overlay`, `gm-neural-library-overlay`, `gm-new-frequency-overlay`, `gm-vocab-overlay`, `gm-concede-overlay`, `gm-deck-panel`, `gm-how-to-overlay` (GM); `ss-settings-overlay`, `ss-dossier-overlay`, `ss-how-to-overlay` (SS); `ygi-help-tip-overlay` (YGI); `lttp-smalltalk-overlay`, `lttp-tip-overlay`, `lttp-help-tip-overlay` (LTTP); `sound-overlay` (global). Verified by scripted token-exact sweep of `resetToLobby()` + all delegated reset bodies (13 June 2026); `ygi-help-tip-overlay` + the two LTTP tip overlays added by the Phase 3 YGI/LTTP read (the original scripted sweep matched only `lttp-smalltalk-overlay` for LTTP).
**Why it matters:** In Lobby Mode, `resetToLobby()` can fire while any overlay is open (host taps end-game, or client confirms the host-disconnected overlay) — the stale overlay then survives on top of the lobby, the DYB BUG-05 ghost-interceptor class. LI5, GM, SS, and LTTP are all multiplayer-capable, so every listed overlay is reachable in this window.
**Fix:** Add a `style.display = 'none'` for each listed overlay to `resetToLobby()` (or to the owning game's delegated reset function); `sound-overlay` can be added to the engine's own teardown block.
**Verify:** Re-run the sweep: every `fixed inset-0` overlay id in `index.html` appears (token-exact or via template-literal loop) in `resetToLobby()` + delegate bodies; manually open GM settings on a client device, kill the host, confirm OK → lobby shows with no stale overlay.
**Rule violated:** `phase-audit.md` Protocol C Part 2 (`resetToLobby()` teardown row); DYB BUG-05 lesson

### [BUG] BLD — lobby has no `getMinPlayers` at all; engine default allows a 2-player start (role table starts at 5)

**Where:** `js/engine-multiplayer.js` — `MP_GAME_CONFIGS.bld` (lines ~206–212) and the fallback `mpActiveGameConfig?.getMinPlayers?.() ?? 2` (line ~1471)
**What:** The BLD config defines `getMaxPlayers: () => 10` but no `getMinPlayers`, so the lobby falls back to the engine default of **2**. `BLD_ROLE_TABLE` and `BLD_GROUP_TABLE` in `bld.js` have no row below 5 (the game is designed for 5–10; `game-identities.md` documents min 5). (Phase 2 of this audit logged this as `getMinPlayers: () => 4` — that was a misread of GTH's neighbouring entry; reality is the field is absent entirely.)
**Why it matters:** A 2–4 player start looks up `BLD_ROLE_TABLE[count]` → `undefined`, crashing role assignment or silently producing a broken game for all devices.
**Fix:** Add `getMinPlayers: () => 5` to the BLD entry of `MP_GAME_CONFIGS`.
**Verify:** Host a BLD lobby with 4 joined players — the start CTA must stay disabled; with 5 it enables.
**Rule violated:** `game-identities.md` § Game 11 Bailed (Min players: 5)

### [BUG] PASS — `MP_GAME_CONFIGS.pass` missing display fields; mode screen renders "undefined"

**What:** The PASS config has a stray `gameId: 'pass'` key (read by nothing) and is missing the four display fields every other game defines: `gameName`, `emoji`, `ptpLabel`, `brandBtnClass`. `mpShowModeScreen()` unconditionally writes all four into the mode screen — and PASS's menu Play CTA does route through `mpShowModeScreen('pass')` (`pass.js` line ~1289).
**Why it matters:** Every PASS multiplayer entry shows a mode screen with "undefined" as the emoji, "undefined" as the game name, a CTA labelled "undefined", and a CTA `className` containing the literal string `undefined` (no background colour — white text on white).
**Fix:** Add `gameName: 'Pass'`, `emoji: '🃏'`, `ptpLabel: 'Deal Me In'`, `brandBtnClass: 'bg-zinc-900 hover:bg-zinc-800'` to the PASS entry and delete the stray `gameId` key.
**Verify:** Tap Pass → Deal Me In from the lobby: mode screen shows 🃏 / "Pass" and a black branded CTA reading "Deal Me In".
**Rule violated:** `ui-style.md` § Per-game brand reference (PASS row); `logic-engine.md` § Multiplayer checklist (MP_GAME_CONFIGS entry)

### [BUG] LI5 — cancelling a quit from the gatekeeper screen starts a phantom turn timer

**Where:** `js/games/li5.js` — `hideQuitConfirm()` / `btn-gatekeeper-exit` listener
**What:** `btn-gatekeeper-exit` opens `quit-overlay`; the shared `btn-quit-cancel` handler calls `hideQuitConfirm()`, which unconditionally restarts the turn timer (`if (!isPaused) startTimer()`) even though no turn is running on the gatekeeper. The timer ticks audibly in the background; if `timeLeft` reaches 0 it fires `endTurn()` → re-shows the previous turn's stale Report Card → confirming it double-advances the team rotation.
**Why it matters:** Phantom tick sounds at minimum; a skipped team turn and duplicated match-log entries at worst.
**Fix:** Restart the timer only when the quit overlay was opened from `screen-active-play` — e.g. record the opener in `showQuitConfirm()`/the gatekeeper listener, or guard on the visible screen before `startTimer()`.
**Verify:** Gatekeeper → ✕ → "Keep going!" → no tick sounds, no timer running (wait >90s to confirm no spontaneous Report Card).
**Rule violated:** — (logic bug)
**Logged:** `li5-implementation-notes.md` L7

### [BUG] GM — Lobby Mode near-sync round is silently discarded

**Where:** `js/games/great-minds.js` — `gmMpResolveRound()`
**What:** With Resonance Tolerance = Resonant, a near-sync pair (e.g. "dog" / "dogs") takes the `isNearSync` branch, which calls *neither* `gmHandleMatch()` nor `gmHandleMismatch()`: the round is never logged, `gmCurrentPair` / `gmPrevRoundWords` never update, and the host's result screen shows stale previous-round content (blank on round 1). Clients render it as a normal mismatch but with the unchanged pair.
**Why it matters:** The round vanishes from Psychic Echoes, the next round replays the same pair, and host/client screens disagree — in the host's own words in the code, near-sync was meant to be "treated as mismatch for now" but the mismatch handler is never invoked.
**Fix:** In the `isNearSync` case, either call `gmHandleMismatch()` (minimal fix matching the comment's intent) or show the Near-Sync overlay host-side and broadcast the decision (full-feature fix).
**Verify:** MDLM lobby, Resonant tolerance, submit "dog"/"dogs" → both devices show a coherent result, the round appears in Psychic Echoes, and the next round uses the two clues as the new pair.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Interceptor Pattern (host must resolve and broadcast consistent state)
**Logged:** `gm-implementation-notes.md` G4

### [BUG] Suite-wide — `mpLockSync()` is a no-op for all 8 Phase-22 games (`btn-mp-action` never applied)

**Where:** `index.html` (only BLD/GTH/DYB/PASS buttons carry `btn-mp-action`) + `js/engine-multiplayer.js` (`syllySyncLocked` is written at lines 524/533 but read nowhere)
**What:** The sync lock works exclusively through the `.btn-mp-action` CSS class, and none of LI5/GM/SS/JEC/YGI/LTTP/NAT/DSD applies it to any submit button; `window.syllySyncLocked` itself gates nothing. Calling `mpLockSync()` in those games disables no buttons. JEC's prep submit self-protects (manual `pointer-events-none`); the others don't.
**Why it matters:** Worst concrete case is SS: double-tapping "Confirm Code" sends two `SS_DECODE_SUBMIT` ACTIONs and the Host runs `ssResolve()` twice — double token/misfire increments on the authoritative device (wrong game outcome). Other games risk duplicate ACTIONs with milder effects.
**Fix:** Add `btn-mp-action` to every submittable multiplayer button in the eight Phase-22 games (Node script for the bulk `index.html` pass), or make `mpSendEnvelope` drop ACTION sends while `syllySyncLocked` is true (single-point fix; still add the class for the visual grey-out).
**Verify:** In an SS lobby session, double-tap Confirm Code rapidly — Host resolves exactly once; greyed button visible during sync.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Sync Lock + `definitions.md` § `btn-mp-action`
**Logged:** `ss-implementation-notes.md` S10

### [BUG] SS — Lobby Mode client double-applies resolution (inflated scoreboard + duplicated journal entry)

**Where:** `js/engine-multiplayer.js` — `SS_RESOLUTION` SYNC handler (line ~1351)
**What:** The handler assigns the Host's post-increment `tokens`/`misfires`/clue histories/`roundHistory`, then calls `ssResolve()`, which increments tokens/misfires again, pushes a duplicate `ssRoundHistory` entry, and re-archives the clues.
**Why it matters:** The client's resolution screen shows one extra token/misfire whenever one was scored, and the final round appears twice in the client's Mission Journal at gameover. (Self-corrects on the next SYNC; Host state and win decision unaffected.)
**Fix:** Split `ssResolve()` into resolve + render halves; the SYNC handler calls only the render half against the payload state (mirror of `gmMpDisplayResult` pattern).
**Verify:** TLM round with an interception — client resolution scoreboard matches Host exactly; client gameover Mission Journal has no duplicated half.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Interceptor Pattern (clients apply resolved state, never re-resolve)
**Logged:** `ss-implementation-notes.md` S9

### [BUG] SS — multiplayer guards assume exactly 2 devices; MDLM roster permits up to `ssPlayerCount × 2`

**Where:** `js/games/secret-signals.js` (vault-done, intercept/decode submit guards using `mpMyPlayerIdx` as a team index) + `js/engine-multiplayer.js` (`SS_VAULT_DATA` broadcast, `MP_GAME_CONFIGS.ss.getMaxPlayers`)
**What:** Every SS lobby-mode guard treats `mpMyPlayerIdx` as a team index (0/1). With more than 2 devices: devices idx ≥ 2 can never submit anything (`ssMpVaultReady[2]` etc.), and the broadcast `SS_VAULT_DATA` SYNC delivers Team B's vault to every client — including extra Team A devices (the docs' "targeted write" claim was wrong; corrected June 2026). `mpSerialiseSettings('ss')` also omits `ssSelectedCategories`, and client vault rerolls send no ACTION (Host's copy of Team B's vault goes stale).
**Why it matters:** An MDLM SS lobby with 3+ devices soft-locks at the vault stage and leaks vault keywords across teams.
**Fix:** Either cap SS lobbies at 2 devices (`getMaxPlayers: () => 2`, drop `'mdlm'` or treat it as TLM-equivalent) — the minimal honest fix — or add device→team translation to every guard plus a targeted vault write.
**Verify:** SS MDLM lobby with 3 devices either cannot start (cap) or all devices can play their team's turns with no cross-team vault exposure.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § MDLM missing-handler audit; `game-identities.md` § SS Multiplayer (corrected)
**Logged:** `ss-implementation-notes.md` S11

### [BUG] SS — Intel Phase (Sylly Mode) unsupported in Lobby Mode; client device crashes on Team B's turn

**Where:** `js/games/secret-signals.js` — Intel Phase functions (no MP branches) + `ss-endgame-splash` Phase 2 button
**What:** Phase 2 has zero MP packets. After `SS_ENDGAME` both devices show the Phase 2 button; each runs the pass-the-phone Intel Phase locally. The client never receives Team A's vault (`ssVaultA` is `[]`), so `ssIntelTargetVault()[idx].word` throws the moment Team B's guessing turn starts on the client.
**Why it matters:** Multiplayer + Sylly Mode = client-side crash mid-endgame; even before the crash, the two devices run divergent intel phases.
**Fix:** Short-term: force `ssIntelSyllyMode = false` when `syllyMultiplayerMode !== 'single'` (and hide the toggle's effect in lobby sessions). Long-term: host-device-only intel with a client standby screen, or full packet support.
**Verify:** TLM game with Sylly Mode ON reaches endgame — client either never sees the Phase 2 button or shows a standby; no console error.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Missing handler audit
**Logged:** `ss-implementation-notes.md` S12

### [BUG] JEC — client-side Sous Chef merges are unguarded in Lobby Mode

**Where:** `js/games/jec.js` — `jecHandleOversightTap()` / `jecApplyMerge()`
**What:** Oversight tap handlers are wired on every device when the setting is on; `jecApplyMerge()` only adds a broadcast when host. A client merging two cards mutates its local frequency/display/poison state with no ACTION sent — the impl-notes claim "clients cannot initiate merges" is documentation, not code.
**Why it matters:** The client's sifting view silently diverges from the table; scores stay correct (Host computes them) but players argue over different boards.
**Fix:** In `jecHandleOversightTap()`, early-return when `window.syllyMultiplayerMode === 'client'` (and hide the oversight hint on clients).
**Verify:** MDLM client taps two sift cards — nothing happens; host merge still propagates via `JEC_MERGE`.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Interceptor Pattern
**Logged:** `jec-implementation-notes.md` J3

### [BUG] JEC — sifting/tally CTAs not host-gated; clients can run divergent rounds

**Where:** `js/games/jec.js` — `btn-jec-sifting-proceed` / `btn-jec-tally-next` listeners; `js/engine-multiplayer.js` — `JEC_NEXT_ROUND` handler
**What:** Neither CTA checks for client mode. A client tapping "The Taste Test!" runs `jecCalcRoundScores()` locally (mutating `jecScores`, duplicating a `jecRoundLog` entry) and self-navigates; "Next Course" runs `jecStartRound()` locally, popping the client's own word pool and flashing a wrong order word until `JEC_ORDER` lands. The `JEC_NEXT_ROUND` handler causes the same transient even on well-behaved clients (full `jecStartRound()` instead of waiting for `JEC_ORDER`).
**Why it matters:** A client can run ahead of the table with self-computed (and double-logged) scores; every round start briefly shows the wrong word on clients.
**Fix:** Gate both CTAs host-only (clients show a disabled "Waiting for the Head Chef…" label — GTH host-gate pattern), and reduce the `JEC_NEXT_ROUND` handler to a no-op/waiting state, letting `JEC_ORDER` drive the client's round start.
**Verify:** MDLM client taps Taste Test / Next Course — nothing happens; round advances only on host tap; no wrong-word flash on clients.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Host-gate screens before timed phases (pattern); § Interceptor Pattern
**Logged:** `jec-implementation-notes.md` J4

### [BUG] YGI — Lobby Mode double-pushes the round log; malformed entry crashes the gameover carousel

**Where:** `js/games/ygi.js` — vote-resolution host path (line ~561) + `ygiShowResults()` (line ~694); `js/engine-multiplayer.js` — `YGI_VOTE_SUBMIT` host path (line ~965) + `YGI_VERDICT` client handler (line ~980)
**What:** In MP, the host pushes a round-log entry during vote resolution *and then* calls `ygiShowResults()`, which pushes its own entry — so `ygiRoundLog` gets two entries per round. The manual push is also malformed: `prompt` is the prompt **object** (not `.text`) and `entries` lacks the `name/pts/isGhost/isWinner` fields. The client sets `ygiRoundLog = p.roundLog` then also calls `ygiShowResults()` (another push). The single-device path is correct (`ygiComputeAndShowResults()` does not push; only `ygiShowResults()` does).
**Why it matters:** The gameover carousel indicator shows a doubled count; navigating "prev" lands on a malformed entry where `ygiRenderRoundLog()` calls `entry.prompt.replace('[ ]', …)` on an object → **TypeError** that kills the carousel. MP-only.
**Fix:** Remove the manual `ygiRoundLog.push()` from both host paths; let `ygiShowResults()` own the push and build the SYNC `roundLog` after calling it. On the client, assign `p.roundLog` and skip the local push (or ignore the payload and push locally) — never both.
**Verify:** Play a 3-round MDLM YGI game → gameover carousel reads "1 / 3" (not "1 / 6") and "prev"/"next" navigate all three rounds without a console error.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Interceptor Pattern (clients apply resolved state, never re-derive)
**Logged:** `ygi-implementation-notes.md` Y3

### [BUG] YGI — Sudden Death (Solo Take tie-break) is not multiplayer-aware

**Where:** `js/games/ygi.js` — `ygiStartSuddenDeath()` / `ygiShowSDPassGate()` / `ygiShowSDInput()` / `ygiResolveSuddenDeath()` (no MP branches)
**What:** When `ygiDecider === 'only-one'` (Solo Take) and the final standings tie, the game runs a pass-the-phone sudden-death flow with zero ACTION/SYNC packets. In MDLM each device independently reaches `ygiShowGameOver()` (results-next is not host-gated) and runs its own local SD.
**Why it matters:** Conditional (Solo Take + a tie), but in MDLM the sudden-death is unplayable/divergent — same class as SS Intel-Phase S12.
**Fix:** Short-term: force `ygiDecider = 'close-enough'` (Split Take) when `syllyMultiplayerMode !== 'single'`. Long-term: host-driven SD with ACTION submissions + a `YGI_SUDDEN_DEATH` SYNC.
**Verify:** MDLM YGI with Solo Take, force a points tie → no divergent/locked SD; either Split Take is enforced or all devices follow one host-driven SD.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Missing handler audit
**Logged:** `ygi-implementation-notes.md` Y4

### [BUG] YGI — `btn-ygi-results-next` not host-gated; clients advance the round locally

**Where:** `js/games/ygi.js` — `btn-ygi-results-next` listener (line ~711) → `ygiStartRound()`
**What:** The results "Next Situation →" button runs `ygiStartRound()` on whichever device taps it. On a client this pops the client's own independently-shuffled `ygiPromptPool` and shows `screen-ygi-prompt` with the wrong situation until the host's `YGI_ROUND_START` SYNC overwrites it.

**Verify:** MDLM client taps Next Situation — nothing happens; round advances only on host tap; no wrong-prompt flash.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Interceptor Pattern
**Logged:** `ygi-implementation-notes.md` Y5

### [BUG] LTTP — MDLM plan narrowing / advancement is never synced (devices diverge after lap 1)

**Where:** `js/engine-multiplayer.js` — `LTTP_MESSAGE_SEND` host handler (line ~1415); `js/games/lttp.js` — `lttpNarrowHighlights()` (line ~995), `lttpSelectPlayer()` lap-completion branch (lines ~960–989)
**What:** Only the messaging loop has packets. The host's `LTTP_MESSAGE_SEND` handler pushes history + advances `lttpActiveIdx` + broadcasts `LTTP_MESSAGE_INTERRUPT`, but never runs the lap-completion logic — so when a *client* completes a lap the host never narrows highlights or advances `lttpPlan`. The lap-completing client narrows locally but its plan-update screen is immediately clobbered by the interrupt-dismiss → `lttpShowChat()`. And `lttpNarrowHighlights()` picks decoys via `shuffle()`, so independent per-device narrowing would diverge anyway. There is no `LTTP_PLAN_UPDATE` SYNC.
**Why it matters:** After the first full lap, devices show different remaining locations and the plan can stall — LTTP's primary multiplayer mode is partially broken mid-game. (Confirm in browser; Phase 28 MDLM testing likely only exercised the first lap's messaging.)
**Fix:** Make the host own lap completion: host computes narrowing once and broadcasts the resulting `lttpHighlights`/`lttpFadedCells`/`lttpPlan` as an `LTTP_PLAN_UPDATE` SYNC (send the resolved sets, not a shuffle seed). Clients apply and render; no client-side narrowing.
**Verify:** MDLM LTTP, complete a full lap with a *client* as the last asker → all devices advance to the same Plan and show identical highlighted cells.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Interceptor Pattern (host resolves and broadcasts consistent state)
**Logged:** `lttp-implementation-notes.md` L5

### [BUG] LTTP — MDLM guess phase + gameover have no MP packets

**Where:** `js/games/lttp.js` — `lttpStartGuessPhase()`, `lttpShowGuess()`/pin+vote screens, `lttpComputeAndShowGameover()` (no MP branches)
**What:** The entire Plan-4 endgame (pin/vote/scoring/reveal) carries zero ACTION/SYNC. In MDLM it either never starts on client devices (when the host completes the final lap) or runs a divergent local pass-the-phone flow.
**Why it matters:** The game cannot be completed correctly in its primary multiplayer mode — exact mirror of the SS Intel-Phase gap (S12).
**Fix:** Host-driven endgame: clients submit pins/votes via ACTION; host resolves and broadcasts `LTTP_GAMEOVER` with winner + reason + all votes. (Or document MDLM as messaging-only and hard-gate the endgame to the host.)
**Verify:** MDLM LTTP reaches Plan 4 → all devices enter the guess phase, submit, and land on the same gameover result with no console error.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Missing handler audit
**Logged:** `lttp-implementation-notes.md` L6

### [BUG] NAT — Selection voting + Last Stand are not MP-distributed (every device runs its own local vote)

**Where:** `js/games/nat.js` — `natStartVoting()`, `btn-nat-sel-start` / `btn-nat-sel-consensus-submit` listeners, `natSubmitVote()`, `natSubmitMoleGuess()`, `natBiologistVerdict()`; `js/engine-multiplayer.js` — `NAT_SELECTION` / `NAT_TALLY` handlers (lines ~1069–1084)
**What:** The observation loop is fully synced and the clue reveal (`NAT_SELECTION`) + final scores (`NAT_TALLY`) are broadcast, but the voting phase between them carries no packets and no host gate. Tapping "Begin Classification" (`btn-nat-sel-start` → `natStartVoting`) on any device runs the vote locally and applies the peer-review −5 deductions locally; the consensus/independent vote controls, the mole guess, and the Biologist verdict are equally ungated. `natMpVoteReadyCheck` is reset in both the `NAT_MATCH_START` and `NAT_SELECTION` handlers but is read nowhere — the intended per-device vote collection was scaffolded and never built.
**Why it matters:** In MDLM each device runs a divergent local vote → eviction → Last Stand, and the single-device pass-the-phone independent-vote flow expects the *holding* device to enter votes for every (remote) player — unplayable as designed. The host's `NAT_TALLY` makes the end scores converge, but the vote experience is broken. Same class as SS Intel-Phase (S12), YGI Sudden Death (Y4), LTTP guess/gameover (L6).
**Fix:** Short-term: hard-gate the Selection→Last-Stand flow to the host (clients show a "Waiting for the field team…" standby after `NAT_SELECTION`). Long-term: per-device vote collection — each device submits its own player's vote via a `NAT_VOTE` ACTION, host aggregates against `natMpVoteReadyCheck.every(Boolean)`, then drives eviction/Last-Stand with ACTION submissions from the actual Mole/Biologist devices.
**Verify:** MDLM NAT reaches the Selection → all client devices either show a host-driven standby or submit exactly one vote each; eviction, mole guess, and verdict happen once (host-authoritative) and all devices land on the same tally.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § MDLM missing-handler audit
**Logged:** `nat-implementation-notes.md` N2

### [BUG] DSD — Nuclear Mine ends the game without broadcasting `DSD_GAMEOVER` (spectator stranded)

**Where:** `js/games/dsd.js` — `dsdResolveHit()` Nuclear Mine branch (line ~912, `setTimeout(() => dsdShowGameover(), 2600)`) vs `dsdAdvanceTurn()` (line ~959, the only `DSD_GAMEOVER` broadcaster)
**What:** A Nuclear Mine detonation is terminal inside `dsdResolveHit` and jumps straight to `dsdShowGameover()` after a 2.6s delay, bypassing `dsdAdvanceTurn()` → `dsdCheckVictory()`. `dsdShowExecution()` still broadcasts `DSD_EXECUTION_RESULT` (grid + −1000 Valour), but no path broadcasts `DSD_GAMEOVER`. Danger Level is serialised (`mpSerialiseSettings('dsd')`), so a Lobby Mode game can reach this state.
**Why it matters:** The active crew device shows gameover via its own local `setTimeout` (host, or client execution preview), masking the gap there — but the non-active **spectator (TLM) / standby (MDLM)** device only receives `DSD_EXECUTION_RESULT` and is stranded on the spectator/execution screen, never reaching the gameover screen. Normal victory (via `dsdAdvanceTurn`) is unaffected.
**Fix:** In the Nuclear Mine branch, when `window.syllyMultiplayerMode === 'host'`, broadcast the `DSD_GAMEOVER` SYNC (valour + grid + turnLog) alongside scheduling the local `dsdShowGameover()` — mirror the broadcast `dsdAdvanceTurn()` already does for normal victory.
**Verify:** TLM DSD with Danger Level = Nuclear Mine; active crew arms a Nuclear Mine → both the active device and the spectator device advance to the gameover screen.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Interceptor Pattern (host must broadcast every terminal state)
**Logged:** `dsd-implementation-notes.md` Bug Index (Nuclear Mine gameover)

### [BUG] GTH — Case-screen `[?]` button has no handler; How to Play is unreachable during MDLM play

**Where:** `index.html` — `#btn-gth-how-to-case` (Case screen header, line ~5997); `js/games/gth.js` (no listener exists)
**What:** The `[?]` button on `screen-gth-case` has id `btn-gth-how-to-case`, but `gth.js` only wires `btn-gth-how-to` (the disorder-reveal screen's button). `btn-gth-how-to-case` has no `addEventListener` anywhere, so tapping it does nothing. Critically, `screen-gth-disorder-reveal` (the one with the working `[?]`) is only shown on the single-device dev path — MDLM goes Patient Intake → Canvas → Case directly (`gthStartPhase1Drawing()` → `gthShowCanvas()`), skipping disorder-reveal. So in real MDLM play the Case screen's dead `[?]` is the only help button a player can reach.
**Why it matters:** How to Play is effectively unreachable mid-game in the only mode GTH ships in (MDLM). Violates the universal "[?] opens How to Play on the main gameplay screen" rule.
**Fix:** Add a listener for `btn-gth-how-to-case` mirroring `btn-gth-how-to` (scroll-reset `.overlay-data-inner` + show `gth-how-to-overlay`). One-line addition in `gth.js` DOMContentLoaded block.
**Verify:** In an MDLM session, on the Case screen tap `[?]` → the How to Play overlay opens.
**Rule violated:** `ui-style.md` § Global UI Protocol (Help icon `[?]`); `phase-audit.md` Protocol A §4 (`[?]` opens How to Play on main gameplay screen)
**Logged:** `gth-implementation-notes.md` Bug Index

### [BUG] DYB — gameover standings invert the loser ranking (double-reverse cancels out)

**Where:** `js/games/dyb.js` — `dybShowGameover()` (lines ~833 + ~837)
**What:** Line 833 builds `const order = [...data.eliminationOrder].reverse();` (correct ranking order — last-eliminated first), but line 837 then spreads `...order.reverse()`, which reverses `order` in place *again* and nets back to the raw `eliminationOrder`. Result: `positions = [winnerIdx, ...eliminationOrder]`, so the **first-eliminated** player is shown as runner-up and the **last-eliminated** as wooden spoon — exactly backwards.
**Why it matters:** Player-visible wrong final standings every game with 3+ players. game-identities states "Rank at end = reverse elimination order (last eliminated = 2nd place)".
**Fix:** Drop the second reverse — use `const positions = [data.winnerIdx, ...order];` (where `order` is the already-reversed copy from line 833).
**Verify:** 4-player game; eliminate players in order A, B, C with D winning → standings read D (1st), C (2nd), B (3rd), A (4th).
**Rule violated:** `game-identities.md` § Game 10 Dicey Bluffs (Scoring/Elimination note)
**Logged:** `dyb-implementation-notes.md` BUG-06

### [BUG] DYB — Phantom die never reveals its face, even at the showdown

**Where:** `js/games/dyb.js` — `dybDieHTML()` phantom branch (lines ~990–992)
**What:** The phantom case sets `display = '?'` unconditionally inside the `visible` branch, so a phantom die shows "?" everywhere — including `dybRenderAllHandsOnShowdown()` (called with `visible = true`). The how-to (`index.html` line ~6593) promises Phantom dice "hide their face until the showdown", implying a reveal that never happens. `dybComputeRealCount()` still counts the phantom at its real rolled value, so the tally includes a die whose value no one can see.
**Why it matters:** In a bluffing game built on verifying the real count at showdown, an unverifiable die undermines trust; the how-to and the code disagree.
**Fix:** In `dybDieHTML`, when `visible` is true (showdown/spirit reveal) render the phantom's real face (`faces[val-1]`) instead of "?". Keep "?" only while the owner holds it during play. (Alternatively reword the how-to if permanent concealment is the intent — but reveal is the better fix.)
**Verify:** Sylly Mode game with a phantom die in play; at the showdown the phantom shows its real pip, and the count is auditable.
**Rule violated:** how-to / code consistency (`index.html` DYB how-to overlay)
**Logged:** `dyb-implementation-notes.md` BUG-07

### [BUG] DYB — eliminated players are pulled back to the Shake screen each round (`DYB_NEXT_SHAKE` has no guard)

**Where:** `js/games/dyb.js` — `DYB_NEXT_SHAKE` SYNC handler (lines ~1150–1155) → `dybInitShake()` (no eliminated guard)
**What:** BUG-02 guarded `DYB_SHAKE_ACTIVE` for eliminated devices, but `DYB_NEXT_SHAKE` (sent by `dybAdvanceFromShowdown()`) calls `dybInitShake()` on every device with no `dybActivePlayers.includes(mpMyPlayerIdx)` check. An eliminated player is therefore navigated to `screen-dyb-shake` and sits there with a live-looking "Shake 'Em Up" button until `DYB_SPIRIT_SHAKE` arrives — which only fires after *all* surviving players have rolled.
**Why it matters:** Eliminated players spend the whole roll-collection window on a screen they shouldn't see, and can tap roll/ready (harmless to logic — host's every-check ignores them — but clearly wrong UX). The Spirit Board is supposed to be their home from the next shake onward.
**Fix:** In the `DYB_NEXT_SHAKE` handler, after updating `activePlayers`/`diceInHand`, branch: if `!dybActivePlayers.includes(mpMyPlayerIdx)` route to `dybShowSpiritBoard()` (and skip `dybInitShake()`'s screen show) instead of the Shake screen.
**Verify:** 3-player MDLM; eliminate one player; on the next shake the eliminated device stays on the Spirit Board rather than flashing the Shake screen.
**Rule violated:** `game-identities.md` § Game 10 (eliminated players routed to Spirit Board from next Shake onwards)
**Logged:** `dyb-implementation-notes.md` BUG-08

### [BUG] PASS — Abyss never detonates mid-trick (Sylly Mode core mechanic incomplete)

**Where:** `js/games/pass.js` — `passProcessPlay()` (only the `hand.length === 0` branch calls `passResolveAbyssDetonation()`)
**What:** The headline Sylly Mode rule — "play a Bomb or Sequence and the Abyss detonates, dealing its cards clockwise to opponents" — only fires when that Bomb/Sequence *also empties the player's hand* (the round-winning play). A Bomb/Sequence played mid-trick does nothing to the Abyss; it only ever grows on passes until a Fracture (13). The comment "Abyss mid-trick detonation: table cleared by Bomb or Sequence" flags the intent but no code implements it.
**Why it matters:** The marquee Sylly mechanic is effectively dead in normal play — detonation is a rare side-effect of winning rather than the active, repeatable "set off the pile" play the how-to overlay promises. Players who enable The Abyss get a watered-down version of the advertised game.
**Fix:** In `passProcessPlay()`, immediately after a valid combo is laid and before the hand-empty check, add: `if (passSyllyMode && passAbyss.length > 0 && new Set(['Triplet','Quad','DoubleJoker','Sequence','DoubleSequence']).has(combo.type)) { detonate clockwise with the playing player exempt (passResolveAbyssDetonation(playerIdx)) and broadcast PASS_ABYSS_DRAFT with trigger:'detonation' }`. Then continue the normal turn advance.
**Verify:** 3-player MDLM, Sylly Mode on; pass a few times to seed the Abyss, then play a Triplet that does NOT empty your hand — the Abyss should distribute to opponents and clear, and the opponents' hand counts should rise.
**Rule violated:** `game-identities.md` § Game 12 Sylly Mode — The Abyss
**Logged:** `pass-implementation-notes.md` BUG-01

### [BUG] PASS — client "rounds won" tally resets to zero every round

**Where:** `js/games/pass.js` — `PASS_GAME_START` SYNC handler (`passRoundsWon = Array(passPlayerCount).fill(0)`, line ~1093) + `PASS_ROUND_END` handler passing local `passRoundsWon` to `passShowGameover()` (line ~1158)
**What:** `passStartRound()` re-broadcasts `PASS_GAME_START` at the start of *every* round; the client handler zeroes `passRoundsWon` each time, so a client's gameover "N rounds won" subline reflects only the final round, not the cumulative total. The host never resets it in `passStartRound()`, so the host stays correct; only clients diverge. The client gameover also ignores the authoritative `payload.roundsWon` the host sends in `PASS_ROUND_END`.
**Why it matters:** Wrong stat shown to every non-host player at gameover, and rounds-won is the secondary tie-break in the client's local standings sort (matters when chip totals tie).
**Fix:** Either (a) broadcast the existing-but-unused `PASS_NEXT_ROUND` for rounds 2+ (its handler correctly does not touch `passRoundsWon`), or (b) remove the `passRoundsWon` reset from the `PASS_GAME_START` handler and have the client gameover consume `payload.roundsWon` (host already sends it when `matchOver`).
**Verify:** 3-player MDLM, 3-round match; finish the match and confirm a client's gameover shows the same rounds-won counts as the host.
**Rule violated:** `logic-engine.md` § Multiplayer Sync Module (host is authoritative; clients must not recompute divergent state)
**Logged:** `pass-implementation-notes.md` BUG-02

### [BUG] data/words.json — duplicate `id` "objects-053" (two different words share one id)

**Where:** `data/words.json` — `objects-053` appears twice: "Walkie-Talkie" (difficulty 2) and "Stapler" (difficulty 1). The objects category also has no `objects-039` — that slot is missing.
**What:** Two distinct entries carry the same `id`. The objects category runs 001–055 (55 entries) but with `objects-053` duplicated and `objects-039` absent. Stapler is the stray — it was almost certainly meant to be `objects-039`.
**Why it matters:** Violates the hard "id must be unique across the entire file" rule (Phase 4A check). No player-facing effect today (words are drawn by `word`/`category`, not `id`), but any id-keyed tooling, dedup, or future content pipeline silently loses one of the two entries — a scaling hazard the audit's "ready to scale" goal exists to prevent.
**Fix:** Re-key the Stapler entry `objects-053` → `objects-039` (the vacant slot). Do not edit `words.json` with the Edit tool for bulk changes — single-line single-element edit is acceptable, but confirm the custom one-entry-per-line serialiser format is preserved (no pretty-print).
**Verify:** `node -e "const d=require('./data/words.json');const s={};let dup=[];d.forEach(w=>s[w.id]?dup.push(w.id):s[w.id]=1);console.log(dup)"` prints `[]`.
**Rule violated:** `definitions.md` § Data Schema (unique `id`); `fable-audit-plan.md` Phase 4A § No duplicate IDs

### [BUG] data/secret_words.json — `world-001` has an 11-word `nono_list` (schema requires exactly 10)

**Where:** `data/secret_words.json` — `world-001` ("Ancient"), `nono_list` = [Throne, End, Destroy, Win, Lose, Main, Building, Health, Base, Tree, Victory] — 11 entries.
**What:** Every other entry in the file (and in `words.json`) carries exactly 10 `nono_list` words; this one has 11.
**Why it matters:** Schema-length violation. Low play impact (Like I'm Five slices the list to 5 or 10 per `settingTabooCount`, so the 11th is never shown), but it breaks the "10 forbidden words" contract and any code that assumes a fixed length.
**Fix:** Drop one redundant word from the list to bring it to 10. "Win"/"Victory"/"Destroy" overlap — removing "Victory" (closest synonym to "Win") is the cleanest trim.
**Verify:** `node -e "const d=require('./data/secret_words.json');console.log(d.filter(w=>w.nono_list.length!==10).map(w=>w.id))"` prints `[]`.
**Rule violated:** `definitions.md` § Data Schema (`nono_list` array of 10); `docs/expansion-guide.md`

### [DOC] Legacy plugins wire all event listeners at top-level script execution — rule/reality conflict

**Where:** `js/games/li5.js`, `js/games/great-minds.js`, `js/games/secret-signals.js`, `js/games/jec.js`, `js/games/ygi.js`, `js/games/dsd.js`, `js/games/bld.js` (top-level — non-compliant). **`js/games/lttp.js`, `js/games/nat.js`, `js/games/gth.js`, `js/games/dyb.js`, and `js/games/pass.js` are the exceptions — they wrap their listeners in `DOMContentLoaded` (compliant).**
**What:** Protocol A §2 requires "no global-scope event listeners — all `addEventListener` calls must live inside an init or start function". LI5, GM, SS, JEC, YGI, DSD, and BLD register their listeners at top-level script execution (DSD and BLD wire only their `.btn-open-sound` buttons inside `DOMContentLoaded`; everything else is top-level); LTTP, NAT, GTH, DYB, and PASS correctly use `DOMContentLoaded`. (Note: of the newer MDLM games only BLD is non-compliant — LTTP/NAT/GTH/DYB/PASS all wrap their listeners; BLD is the lone exception.) The top-level pattern is functionally safe in this SPA (all HTML is parsed before the `<script>` tags run — same guarantee the engine's own top-level `.btn-open-sound` wiring relies on), but it means over half the suite permanently fails a written audit gate.
**Why it matters:** An audit rule that the stable, shipped games can never pass either gets ignored (rot) or triggers needless refactors of working legacy code.
**Fix:** Developer decision: relax the Protocol A §2 wording to "top-level listeners are acceptable given the script-after-markup load order; new games should still prefer `DOMContentLoaded`/init wiring", or schedule a deliberate refactor of the legacy plugins. Do not refactor during the audit (Principle 1).
**Verify:** `phase-audit.md` Protocol A §2 wording matches the decided policy.
**Rule violated:** Audit Principle 3 (reality wins) vs `phase-audit.md` Protocol A §2

### [DOC] data/secret_words.json — 10 entries are missing the `category` key entirely

**Where:** `data/secret_words.json` — 10 entries with NO `category` key: `world-075` (Day Cycle), `world-081` (Disarm), `world-082` (Vector Casting), `world-083` (Forced Movement), `world-084` (Innate Ability), `world-085` (Facet), `world-086` (Bloodstone Active), `world-087` (True Sight), `world-090` (Projectile Speed), `world-095` (Pure Damage). (Phase 4D resolved the Phase-1A flag: the key is absent, not an empty string — `JSON.parse` yields `undefined`, which had shown as a `""`-like distinct category.)
**What:** These 10 entries have the shape `{id, word, nono_list, difficulty}` — the `category` field is omitted. All 424 other entries carry `category` (Heroes / Items / World / Social). By their `world-*` ids and theme they all belong to category `World`.
**Why it matters:** Category-filtered pools silently exclude uncategorised entries. Secret Mode (Dota 2) mostly draws the full bank so normal play is unaffected, but any category-subset draw or the SS category picker loses these 10 silently. Pure data inconsistency rather than a player-visible bug today.
**Fix:** Add `"category": "World"` to all 10 listed entries.
**Verify:** `node -e "const d=require('./data/secret_words.json');console.log(d.filter(w=>!w.category).map(w=>w.id))"` prints `[]`.
**Rule violated:** `definitions.md` § Data Schema

### [DOC] MDLM mid-game quit — room-teardown behaviour is inconsistent across the four MDLM games

**Where:** `js/games/gth.js`, `js/games/dyb.js`, `js/games/bld.js` (quit → game menu, no teardown) vs `js/games/pass.js` (quit → `PASS_MATCH_DISSOLVED` / `PASS_PLAYER_LEFT` + `resetToLobby()`)
**What:** On a mid-game quit, GTH/DYB/BLD navigate to their game menu and leave the Firebase room intact (teardown deferred to a later "← Back to the Box"); PASS instead broadcasts a dissolution and tears the room down immediately, returning all devices to the lobby. PASS's behaviour is the most correct (no leaked room, peers notified) but deviates from the universal "✕ → game menu" rule, and means any single player quitting dissolves the whole PASS match.
**Why it matters:** Four MDLM games, two opposite quit contracts. GTH/DYB/BLD can leave a stale room (and a host who quits doesn't notify clients until they navigate further); PASS can't tolerate a mid-match drop. A future MDLM game has no single pattern to copy.
**Fix:** Developer decision — standardise MDLM mid-game quit on one contract. Recommended: the host's mid-game quit should broadcast `HOST_END_GAME` (or a per-game dissolve) and tear down, like PASS; clients leave individually without dissolving the match where the game can continue short-handed. Then encode the chosen contract in `logic-engine.md` § Multiplayer.
**Verify:** `logic-engine.md` documents the MDLM mid-game quit contract and all four games match it.
**Rule violated:** `ui-style.md` § Global UI Protocol (exit routing) vs `logic-engine.md` § resetToLobby() — currently unreconciled for MDLM
**Logged:** `pass-implementation-notes.md` (quit dissolve note); cross-referenced in GTH/DYB/BLD audit findings (`fable-audit-plan.md` Phase 3)
